meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, and my son found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, with nobody calling me first. Who decided that, and when?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
"Fair." You're comparing forty minutes in class in September with an essay he wrote over a weekend, and calling that evidence? Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in, yes or no?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then show me the version history, with the dates and times on it. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in our meeting that the checker alone proves nothing and took it off the table. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology, a clear answer on whether Owen was heard before the mark was entered, and a copy of the version history you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on whether Owen was heard before the mark went in.
What moved her: Nothing; the dated September writing sample was the right kind of evidence, but it was only described, and the version history was named but never shown, so she had nothing she could check herself.
What cost ground: Twice skipping her direct question about who decided and whether Owen was heard first, which to a litigator looks like the process went wrong and you're avoiding it.
Try next time: In your very first reply, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put the version history on screen with its times so she can read it herself.
